transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (GlacierPoint HoML), Daniel Kim (Infra), Sara Velasquez (Security), Tom Wu (Product)

Summary:
GlacierPoint is evaluating options to move inferencing from a primarily OpenAI-hosted setup (plus some self-hosted vLLM experiments) to either Redwood Hosted for rapid time-to-value, Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, or Redwood Private (VPC) for data governance. Primary concerns: parity with current OpenAI outputs, vLLM/TGI compatibility for some local tooling, encryption/KMS and audit requirements, latency for interactive clinician-facing product, and unit cost. They want benchmarks on their prompt set and a short pilot plan.

Topics:
- Current stack and what they run locally
- Model compatibility: vLLM/TGI -> Redwood variants
- Hosting tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
- Benchmarks and pilot success criteria

Action items (see metadata): Marcus to run perf checks; Alicia to send pricing and docs; schedule VPC deep dive.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, i'm alicia from redwood, this is marcus our solutions engineer. uh quick round okay?
[00:12] Priya: hey i'm priya, head of ml at glacierpoint, we run mostly openai gpt-4.1 and some internal vllm tests for batch preproc, current cost is uh pretty high so we're exploring options.
[00:25] Daniel: daniel here, infra lead. main constraint is we need private networking for phi-sensitive data and we wanna know what a vpc deployment looks like.
[00:36] Alicia: great, that's what we hear a lot. marcus do you want to frame the hosting options quickly?
[00:42] Marcus: sure yeah, basically three lanes: hosted api (fastest to ship, usage pricing), dedicated (reserved gpu pools, predictable throughput, burst configs) and private (vpc or on-prem with control plane options). for parity we can map their openai calls to compatible model variants, and for teams running vllm/tgi we can run compatibility tests — there are some differences in kv cache handling and tokenizer edge cases.
[01:10] Tom: quick q — you said tokenizers can differ? we've seen minor output drift between openai and local vllm runs, is that common?
[01:20] Marcus: yeah small drift is expected, tokenizer implementations, default sampling seeds, and sometimes precision/quantization differences cause it. we aim for eval parity not byte-for-byte identical. typical approach: run your prompt set, capture metrics (perplexity-ish proxies, exact-match, hallucination rates) and then tune a model variant or apply a post-processing alignment layer.
[01:45] Priya: ok good. our chief metric is clinician-facing correctness and response latency below 400 ms on average for short queries, cost target is 60% of our current spend.
[01:58] Alicia: that's super helpful, and doable to objective. for latency bound — hosted often gives lower cold-latency but dedicated with reserved capacity and pre-warmed kv caches can meet stricter SLOs.
[02:15] Sara: security side — do you support customer-managed keys? we need KMS/HSM integration and full audit logs for access to phi. also SSO/SAML and RBAC at a per-team level.
[02:28] Marcus: yes kmS integrations are supported for private and dedicated; hosted supports envelope encryption and we have integrations for major KMS providers. audit logs and token-level tracing are in console; RBAC and sso are supported, we can send the SOC2 pack and integrations doc.
[02:45] Daniel: about data residency — can we pin region? we need eu data residency for some subsets.
[02:52] Alicia: yes region pinning is possible for dedicated and private; hosted has regional endpoints too but dedicated gives stronger guarantees and isolation.
[03:05] Tom: you mentioned vllm and tgi compatibility — we use a custom tgi pipeline for some fine-tuned models, are there known blockers?
[03:15] Marcus: main things to watch for: custom kernels and some TGI plugins that rely on particular runtime hooks. we can usually replicate the inference graph in our runtime but need to validate custom ops. kv cache semantics differ across runtimes — if you rely on incremental decode with nonstandard cache ops we'll want a small emulation test. i'll add compatibility notes and sample config.
[03:45] Priya: perfect. also our bench set has 1200 prompts across triage, summarization, and structured extraction. can you run a run with that?
[03:53] Marcus: yes absolutely, we'll need the dataset and expected outputs and we'll run hosted and dedicated matrix to show latency/cost/quality. do you have perf thresholds?
[04:05] Priya: thresholds: latency <400ms p50 for short queries, p95 <800ms; exact-match for structured fields >92%; hallucination reduction of 30% vs current prod.
[04:20] Alicia: noted. next — procurement: timeline? when would you want to decide?
[04:26] Priya: Q2 budget cycle, ideally pilot in 6 weeks, roll to prod in 3 months if pilot looks good.
[04:33] Alicia: okay that's workable. we'll propose a 6-week pilot on dedicated or private depending on security outcomes.
[04:40] Sara: also need a runbook for incident response and SLA details — can you share SLOs and fallbacks?
[04:48] Marcus: yes we have documented SLOs for hosted and dedicated; we also do automated fallback policies — e.g., route to a cheaper compatible model under heavy load. we'll include that in the playbook.
[05:05] Tom: any migration lift for prompt engineering? our prompts are tuned for openai-ish behaviors.
[05:12] Marcus: some prompt tuning is often required. we offer a prompt alignment phase in the pilot where we test a small set and map outputs then tune system prompts or apply response normalization.
[05:28] Priya: cost — what's the usual delta for dedicated vs hosted? we want to be sure cost target is reachable.
[05:35] Alicia: hosted is pay-as-you-go and easiest; dedicated amortizes GPU costs so for high throughput it's cheaper per token. we'll share a spreadsheet with break-even points.
[05:48] Daniel: network egress for private deployment — we need a way to keep phi in private subnets, do you support air-gapped connectors?
[05:56] Marcus: yes for on-prem we have an air-gapped option, for VPC we can do private peering and customer-managed NAT/egress policies. there are configuration checklists.
[06:12] Sara: does redwood provide a compliance attestation for specific workloads? we need SOC2 plus data processing agreement.
[06:20] Alicia: yes DPA and SOC2 plus special terms can be included in enterprise contracts; we'll share the legal pack.
[06:28] Tom: in terms of rollout strategy, what do you recommend? start with hosted then move to dedicated? or pilot private?
[06:36] Marcus: pragmatic path is hosted for rapid eval, dedicated for production if you need throughput guarantees, private if regulations require it. however if security constraints block hosted we start with dedicated in a VPC.
[06:52] Priya: ok makes sense. we have some models that are fine-tuned with tgi — will fine-tuning artifacts move over easily?
[07:00] Marcus: fine-tuning bundles vary; we can accept model weights in common formats, and for custom TGI fine-tunes we'll validate that runtime ops are supported. sometimes re-export is needed.
[07:15] Alicia: any other blockers?
[07:18] Daniel: curious about observability — token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards? we need to show cost per feature.
[07:26] Marcus: console has token-level breakdown, per-route mlmetrics and latency traces, and per-model dashboards. you can export to prometheus/bigquery.
[07:38] Priya: great. what about caching — do you support prefix or kv caching to reduce cost?
[07:44] Marcus: yes automatic prefix caching and kv cache reuse; we also suggest batching strategies for batch jobs to reduce per-token cost.
[07:58] Tom: any gotchas with hallucination-sensitive tasks like clinical summarization?
[08:05] Marcus: yes you want structured extraction rather than open completions for those, add verification steps, and run quality monitors in the pilot. we have eval tooling for continuous regression alerts.
[08:22] Priya: can we see an example of a fallback policy?
[08:26] Marcus: sure — if p95 latency breaches threshold we route new requests to a smaller model variant with same prompt preambles; http 429s trigger burst capacity if reserved, otherwise fallback to secondary region.
[08:40] Sara: re: encryption — do you store user data? retention policies?
[08:45] Alicia: we support configurable retention and can disable retention for pii. for private you control storage. hosted supports short retention and redaction hooks.
[08:57] Daniel: benchmarks — can you document exact env (gpu types, sequence lengths) when you run our prompts?
[09:03] Marcus: yes we'll deliver a benchmark report with environment, kernel versions, quantization used, and cost calculations.
[09:15] Priya: fine. one more question — do you support function calling / structured output?
[09:21] Marcus: yes, streaming responses, structured output and function/tool calling are supported. we can show examples.
[09:30] Tom: backlog for pilot — what's expected from us?
[09:34] Alicia: you provide prompt set, expected outputs, sample traffic pattern, and a security questionnaire. we'll run the tests and then review.
[09:42] Priya: sounds good. any estimate on pilot pricing?
[09:46] Alicia: we'll propose a fixed price pilot for the 6-week run including engineering support; pricing doc to follow.
[09:54] Sara: can we get a short note on incident escalation contacts and SLO credit policy?
[09:59] Marcus: yes included in the SLA doc.
[10:05] Tom: ok let's recap next steps.
[10:09] Alicia: recap: we will send pricing spreadsheet, SOC2/KMS docs, pilot contract; marcus will take the prompt set and run hosted/dedicated bench and prepare vllm/tgi compatibility notes; schedule vpc deep dive next week.
[10:28] Priya: thanks all.
[10:31] Alicia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
